label: JZ Mock E · Paper 2 · Question 3
knowledgePattern: Compare six conditions imposed on the same real input
solution:
I permits −3<x<3. II gives 0<x<2. In III, the common ratio is 4/2=2, so x=1. In IV, the logarithm domain and its increasing base give 0<x+1<2, hence −1<x<1. V gives x=1 or x=2.

For VI, substitute X=x into the circle equation: Y2=1−x2. Two distinct intersections require 1−x2>0, so again −1<x<1. Each of II–VI therefore implies I.

If any of II–VI were true, at least I and that statement would be true, contradicting exactly one. I can be the sole truth: x=−2 satisfies it and fails all five others. Answer A.

hints.title: Give each statement a number line
hints.body: Work out the allowed values of x for each statement. Write an interval or a short list beside it.
hints.recap: A logarithm needs a positive input before its inequality can be solved.
hints.pitfall: Two distinct circle intersections excludes tangency.

recall.reminder: State the positive logarithm arguments before solving.

hints.title: Look for one set inside another
hints.body: Compare your six sets. If every value making one statement true also makes another true, the first cannot be the only true statement.
hints.recap: Exactly one true statement rules out any choice that forces a second truth.
hints.pitfall: After eliminating choices, check one value that makes only the remaining statement true.
hints.pause: Decide which statement can stand alone.
